mainTopic: The king's Torah reading at הקהל, אגריפס and the people's flattery, and the גמרא's teachings on the sin of flattery
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: הקהל takes place at the start of the festival. Then the גמרא goes through the משנה's description of the king's Torah reading. The ספר תורה is passed up through officials to the king, and אביי explains that this whole chain exists to honor the king. The king may read sitting because the reading was in the עזרת נשים. The חכמים praised אגריפס for standing, and although a king may not give up his honor, standing for a מצוה is different. When אגריפס cried at the words 'you may not appoint a foreigner', the people told him 'you are our brother', and רבי נתן says Israel deserved destruction for that flattery. The גמרא then discusses flattery in general. Its terrible effects are set against a limited permission to flatter רשעים in this world, with a dispute about how to read יעקב's words to עשו. The amud ends with a series of רבי אלעזר's teachings on the punishments of a flatterer. The proof of the last teaching continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The gathering happens at the start of the festival
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier point: the הקהל gathering takes place at the beginning of סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the beginning of the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: These words finish a discussion from the previous section. The conclusion is that הקהל happens at the very start of the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the start of the festival everyone has already come up to ירושלים, so the whole nation is there to hear the king read. That is why the timing points to the opening of the festival.

keyTerms.meaning: the gathering of the whole nation to hear the king read from the Torah

phrases.english: From the beginning of the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵאַתְחַלְתָּא דְּמוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion carried over from the previous section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הקהל takes place at the beginning of the festival.

steps.title: The Torah scroll is passed up the line of officials
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the synagogue attendant hands the ספר תורה to the head of the synagogue, and from there it moves up toward the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the synagogue attendant takes a Torah scroll and gives it to the head of the synagogue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה. This sets up a question about honor that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה the ספר is handed up step by step: attendant, head of the synagogue, the סגן, the כהן גדול, and finally the king. Many lower-ranking people hold it before the king does. That order is what the גמרא is about to analyze.

phrases.english: And the synagogue attendant takes a Torah scroll
and gives it to the head of the synagogue.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַזַּן הַכְּנֶסֶת נוֹטֵל סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ספר תורה passes through several officials before it reaches the king.

steps.title: Proof that a student may be honored in front of his teacher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that this passing order proves you may give honor to a lower person (a student) while a higher person (the teacher) is present.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: we may give honor to a student in the place of the teacher!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to draw a general rule from the משנה. The officials get to hold the ספר first while the king is standing right there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when a greater person is present, you would not honor a lesser person ahead of him. Here the lower officials get the honor of holding the ספר first even though the king is present. So the גמרא suggests that honoring the lesser one is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: in the presence of the teacher

phrases.english: Learn from this:
we give honor to a student
phrases.notes: The 'student' stands for the lower officials, and the 'teacher' stands for the king.

phrases.english: in the place of the teacher!

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from the משנה just quoted.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a student may be honored in his teacher's presence.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The officials hold the ספר תורה before the king.

steps.title: אביי: it is all for the king's honor
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. The whole chain of handing is itself meant to honor the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The whole thing is because of the honor of the king.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the proof. The officials are not really being honored at the king's expense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Passing the ספר through so many ranks shows how high the king is above everyone else. The officials are serving the king's honor, not taking honor for themselves. So nothing can be learned about honoring a student in front of his teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: אמורא who rejects the proof here
all of it, the whole thing

steps.whatToRemember: The passing chain at הקהל proves nothing about honoring a student before his teacher. It is entirely to honor the king.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The whole thing is because of the honor of the king.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כּוּלָּהּ מִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹדוֹ דְּמֶלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof is rejected completely; the case is not about honoring the lesser people.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the officials were being honored, but the chain actually exists to show the king's high rank.

steps.title: The king reads sitting, but אגריפס stood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the king stands to receive the ספר and reads sitting. אגריפס המלך stood to receive it and also read standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the king stands and receives it and reads sitting. King Agrippa stood, received it, and read standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up a question about sitting in the Temple courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual practice is that the king may read sitting down. אגריפס went beyond that and stood for the whole reading. The words 'he stood' hint that he had been sitting before, and that is what the next step will attack.

phrases.english: And the king stands and receives
and reads sitting.
King Agrippa stood up and received
and read standing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַמֶּלֶךְ עוֹמֵד וּמְקַבֵּל וְקוֹרֵא יוֹשֵׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The king may read sitting; אגריפס chose to stand.

steps.title: How could anyone sit in the Temple courtyard?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: if אגריפס 'stood up', he was sitting before. But only kings from בית דוד may sit in the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He stood, which implies he had been sitting? But the Master said: There is no sitting in the courtyard except for kings of the house of David alone, as it says: 'Then King David came and sat before ה׳ and said…'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem. Sitting in the עזרה is forbidden except for kings from בית דוד, and אגריפס was not one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the king normally reads sitting, and אגריפס had been sitting until he stood. Yet a known rule allows only Davidic kings to sit in the עזרה, based on the פסוק about דוד sitting before ה׳. How could the משנה describe sitting there at all?

keyTerms.meaning: kings from the family of דוד

phrases.english: 'Standing' implies that he had been sitting?
But didn't the Master say:
There is no sitting in the courtyard
except for kings of the house of David alone,
as it is said: 'Then King David came'
'and sat before ה׳, and said, etc.'!

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹמֵד מִכְּלָל דְּיוֹשֵׁב? וְהָאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the king sits (and that אגריפס had been sitting).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only Davidic kings may sit in the עזרה, so a non-Davidic king like אגריפס could not have been sitting there.

steps.title: It took place in the עזרת נשים
steps.stepSummary: Using רב חסדא's answer from elsewhere, the גמרא says the הקהל reading took place in the עזרת נשים, where the ban on sitting does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חסדא said: in the Women's Courtyard. Here too, in the Women's Courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The reading was not in the main עזרה but in the עזרת נשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against sitting covers only the inner עזרה. רב חסדא used this answer for a similar problem, and the גמרא applies it here. So the king could sit without breaking any rule.

keyTerms.meaning: אמורא whose answer is borrowed here
the Women's Courtyard, outside the inner courtyard

steps.whatToRemember: The king sat at הקהל because the reading was in the עזרת נשים, where the ban on sitting does not apply.

phrases.english: As Rav Chisda said:
in the Women's Courtyard,
here too, it was in the Women's Courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בְּעֶזְרַת נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the case to a place where the rule does not apply.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reading was in the עזרה, where only Davidic kings may sit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reading was in the עזרת נשים, where sitting is permitted.

steps.title: The חכמים praised אגריפס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the חכמים praised אגריפס for standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages praised him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line from the משנה. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Praising אגריפס suggests that giving up his right to sit was a good thing to do. The next step questions whether a king is even allowed to do that.

phrases.english: And the Sages praised him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשִׁבְּחוּהוּ חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the next words of the משנה about אגריפס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים praised אגריפס for standing.

steps.title: A king may not give up his honor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the חכמים could praise אגריפס. רב אשי taught that even if a נשיא may give up his honor, a king may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They praised him, which implies he acted properly? But רב אשי said: Even according to the one who says a נשיא who gave up his honor, his honor is given up, a king who gave up his honor, his honor is not given up, as it says: 'You shall surely set a king over you,' meaning that his awe should be upon you!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the praise. By standing, אגריפס gave up his royal honor, and a king is not allowed to do that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Praise means the act was right. But רב אשי rules that a king cannot give up his honor, even according to the view that a נשיא can. The פסוק 'שום תשים עליך מלך' teaches that the people must stand in awe of the king, so the honor is not his to give away. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: אמורא who states the rule about a king's honor
the head of the Sanhedrin / leader

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the נשיא and the king. Some hold a נשיא may give up his honor, but everyone agrees a king may not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that a king's honor belongs to the nation's awe of him, so he cannot waive it. That makes the praise of אגריפס a real puzzle.

phrases.english: They praised him, which implies that he acted properly?
But didn't Rav Ashi say:
Even according to the one who says
that a Nasi who gave up his honor,
his honor is given up,
a king who gave up his honor —
his honor is not given up,
as it is said: 'You shall surely set a king over you,'
meaning that his awe should be upon you!

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁבְּחוּהוּ, מִכְּלָל דְּשַׁפִּיר עֲבַד? הָאָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the praise quoted in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's praise of אגריפס for standing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A king may not give up his honor, because the פסוק requires awe of him. So standing was improper and should not have been praised.

steps.title: Giving up honor for a מצוה is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a king may give up his honor when he does it for a מצוה, so the חכמים could rightly praise אגריפס.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מצוה is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 9: how could the חכמים praise אגריפס if a king may not give up his honor? The answer is that standing for a מצוה is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of רב אשי is that a king may not give up his honor. That rule is about ordinary situations. When the king lowers himself out of respect for a מצוה, this is not counted as giving up his honor, so it was right to praise him.

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה is different; the normal rule does not apply here

steps.whatToRemember: A king may not give up his honor, but honoring a מצוה is an exception, so אגריפס deserved the praise.

phrases.english: A מצוה is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִצְוָה שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9 from רב אשי's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule: the ban on a king giving up his honor does not cover an act done for a מצוה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a king may never give up his honor, the חכמים should not have praised אגריפס for standing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Honoring a מצוה is an exception. The praise was proper.

steps.title: Israel punished for flattering אגריפס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's line about אגריפס reaching the פסוק 'you may not appoint a foreigner', and quotes רבי נתן: Israel was sentenced to destruction for flattering him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he reached 'You may not appoint [a foreigner over you]'. It was taught in the name of רבי נתן: At that moment the enemies of Israel deserved destruction, because they flattered אגריפס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. In that line, אגריפס cries when he reads that a foreigner may not be king, and the people tell him 'you are our brother'. Then the גמרא brings a ברייתא that condemns the people's words as flattery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה tells the story as a warm moment, but רבי נתן reads it as a serious sin. אגריפס came from the family of הורדוס, so by the פסוק he was not fit to be king. Telling him 'you are our brother' was flattery, and for that Israel deserved destruction.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You may not appoint' a foreigner as king (דברים 17:15)
'Enemies of Israel', a polite way to refer to Israel itself

steps.confusionAlert: 'שונאי ישראל' does not mean Israel's actual enemies. It is a polite way of saying Israel itself, so the text does not have to say that Israel was sentenced to destruction.

phrases.english: And when he reached 'You may not appoint'.
phrases.notes: דברים 17:15. The משנה goes on to say that he cried, and the people answered, 'You are our brother.'

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Natan:
At that moment they became liable
phrases.notes: 'At that moment' means the moment the people told him 'you are our brother.'

phrases.english: the enemies of Israel, to destruction,
phrases.notes: This is a polite way of talking about Israel itself.

phrases.english: because they flattered Agrippa.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְ״לֹא תוּכַל לָתֵת״. תָּנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of standing and moves on to the next line of the משנה's story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flattering אגריפס by calling him 'our brother' was a sin, and Israel deserved destruction for it.

steps.title: The damage flattery does
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן חלפתא teaches that once flattery took over, justice and people's deeds were ruined, and no one can honestly say his deeds are greater than another's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן חלפתא said: From the day the power of flattery won out, judgments were twisted, deeds were ruined, and a person cannot say to his friend, 'My deeds are greater than yours.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the theme of flattery from the last step. It brings a broader teaching about how much harm flattery causes in the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 condemned one act of flattery. Now we learn what flattery does to a whole society. Judges no longer rule honestly, behavior gets worse, and since everyone praises everyone, no one knows anymore who is truly good.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'fist' of flattery, meaning its power

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Ḥalafta said:
From the day that the power of flattery prevailed,
judgments became corrupted,
and deeds became corrupted,
and a person cannot say to his fellow,
'My deeds are greater than your deeds.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן חֲלַפְתָּא: מִיּוֹם שֶׁגָּבַר אֶגְרוֹפָהּ שֶׁל חֲנוּפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the theme from flattering אגריפס to the harm flattery does in general.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flattery twists justice, ruins behavior, and hides the truth about who is really good.

steps.title: Flattering the wicked is allowed in this world
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה of ארץ ישראל (or רבי שמעון בן פזי) learns from a פסוק in ישעיהו that flattering רשעים is allowed in this world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה of the West (some say רבי שמעון בן פזי) taught: It is allowed to flatter the wicked in this world, as it says, 'A vile person will no longer be called generous, and a scoundrel will not be called noble.' This implies that in this world it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: After so much criticism of flattery, the גמרא brings a teaching that limits it. In this world it is allowed to flatter רשעים, and the proof comes from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ישעיהו speaks about the future and says that 'no longer' will a bad person be called generous. The word 'no longer' implies that until then, meaning in this world, it is allowed. So the strong statements against flattery are not a total ban; in this world there is room to flatter רשעים.
steps.whatToRemember: Flattery is a serious sin, but flattering רשעים is allowed in this world. This is learned from ישעיהו 32:5, which says flattery will stop only in the future.
steps.confusionAlert: This teaching does not cancel רבי נתן's criticism. It only shows that there is a limited area where flattering the wicked is allowed in this world.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda of the West taught,
phrases.notes: 'The West' is how the Babylonian rabbis called ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: and some say it was Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi:
It is permitted to flatter the wicked in this world,
as it says: 'A vile person will no longer be called generous,'
'and a scoundrel will not be called noble.'
This implies that in this world it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר מַעְרְבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two steps that condemn flattery, this one sets out a limited case where it is allowed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flattering רשעים is allowed in this world, as shown by ישעיהו 32:5.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's source: יעקב's words to עשו
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש brings a different פסוק to show that flattering רשעים is allowed: יעקב told עשו that seeing his face was like seeing the face of angels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: We learn it from here: "as one sees the face of God (angels), and you were pleased with me."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second source for the idea from step 13, that you may flatter a רשע in this world. ריש לקיש points to what יעקב said to עשו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב compared seeing עשו to seeing angels, which is strong praise for a רשע. Since יעקב, a צדיק, said this, it shows that flattering a dangerous רשע is allowed. This is a different פסוק from the one in ישעיהו in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: Like seeing the face of angels / God
And you were pleased with me

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: From here:
"As one sees the face of angels, and you were pleased with me."
phrases.notes: בראשית 33:10. יעקב is speaking to עשו.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק for the same rule as step 13: flattering רשעים is allowed in this world.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flattering a רשע is allowed in this world, as יעקב did when he praised עשו.

steps.title: רבי לוי reads יעקב's words as a warning, not flattery
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that ריש לקיש disagrees with רבי לוי. רבי לוי gives a parable: יעקב's words were a hint that he knew angels, meant to scare עשו away from killing him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רבי לוי. For רבי לוי said: The parable of יעקב and עשו, what is it like? It is like a man who invited his friend over, and the guest realized the host wanted to kill him. The guest said: The taste of this dish I am eating is like a dish I ate in the king's palace. The host said to himself: The king knows him! He became afraid and did not kill him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי לוי understands יעקב's words differently than ריש לקיש. רבי לוי explains it with a parable about a guest who mentions the king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, יעקב was flattering עשו. For רבי לוי, יעקב was hinting "I have seen angels", so עשו would be afraid to hurt someone with such powerful connections. On רבי לוי's reading, this פסוק is no proof that flattering a רשע is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: To what is the matter comparable?

steps.confusionAlert: רבי לוי is not saying flattery is forbidden. He only says that this פסוק is about scaring עשו, not about flattering him.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Levi.
For Rabbi Levi said:
The parable of Yaakov and Esav:
What is the matter comparable to?
To a person who invited his friend
and the guest realized that the host wanted to kill him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: טְעַם תַּבְשִׁיל זֶה שֶׁאֲנִי טוֹעֵם
phrases.english: The guest said to him: The taste of this dish that I am tasting
is like a dish that I tasted in the king's house.
The host said to himself: The king knows him!
phrases.notes: The guest is יעקב and the host is עשו.

phrases.english: He was afraid and did not kill him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַבִּי לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that ריש לקיש's reading of the פסוק in step 14 is disputed by רבי לוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יעקב's words to עשו were a hidden warning that he knew angels, meant to make עשו afraid, not flattery.

steps.title: A flatterer brings anger to the world and his prayer is not heard
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a flatterer brings Divine anger to the world, and on top of that his prayers are not answered. Both lessons come from one פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Any person who has flattery in him brings anger to the world, as it says: "And those with flattery in their hearts bring about anger." And not only that, but his prayer is not heard, as it says: "They will not cry out when He binds them."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a set of teachings from רבי אלעזר about how terrible flattery is. This first one gives two punishments for a flatterer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק teaches that flatterers bring anger on the world. The second half teaches that when trouble comes, their crying out to ה׳ does not help. So flattery hurts both the world and the flatterer's own prayers.

keyTerms.meaning: Flattery, falsely praising or giving in to someone
And not only that, but also

steps.whyThisMatters: After hearing that flattering a רשע is sometimes allowed, רבי אלעזר reminds us how serious flattery is in general.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Any person who has flattery in him
brings anger to the world,
as it says: "And those with flattery in their hearts bring about anger."
And not only that, but
his prayer is not heard,
as it says: "They will not cry out when He binds them."
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק in איוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֲנוּפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether flattery is ever allowed to how harmful flattery is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A flatterer brings Divine anger to the world, and his prayer is not heard.

steps.title: A memory sign for רבי אלעזר's teachings on flattery
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a memory sign of six words, each hinting at one of רבי אלעזר's teachings about flattery, in order.
steps.simpleTranslation: (A memory sign: Anger, fetus, גיהנם, in his hand, נדה, exile.)
steps.whatsHappening: This is not a new teaching. The גמרא gives a list of key words to help us remember the order of רבי אלעזר's teachings, which are coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "אף" (anger) matches the teaching we just learned in step 16. The other five words hint at the teachings that will follow. A סימן like this was used to help people learning by heart keep the order straight.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign, a list of hint words to remember the order of teachings
גיהנם, the place of punishment after death

phrases.english: (A memory sign:
phrases.notes: Each word below hints at one teaching of רבי אלעזר about flattery.

phrases.english: Anger, fetus, Gehinnom,
in his hand, niddah, exile.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up the coming list of רבי אלעזר's teachings, starting from the one in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No new ruling. This is a memory aid listing רבי אלעזר's teachings on flattery in order.

steps.title: Even unborn babies curse a flatterer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that even babies still in their mothers' wombs curse a person who flatters. He proves it from a פסוק in משלי by explaining two of its words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Anyone who flatters is cursed even by babies still inside their mothers. The פסוק says that whoever tells a wicked person 'you are righteous' will be cursed by 'עמים' and 'לאומים'. The word 'קוב' means a curse, as in בלעם's words 'לא קבה אל'. The word 'לאום' means unborn babies, as in what was said about יעקב and עשו before they were born: 'ולאם מלאם יאמץ'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another one of רבי אלעזר's teachings about flattery: a flatterer is cursed even by unborn babies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by explaining two words in the פסוק. 'יקבהו' comes from 'קוב', which means cursing, as we see from בלעם. 'לאומים' is read as unborn babies, because the word 'לאם' is used for יעקב and עשו while they were still in רבקה's womb.

keyTerms.meaning: Flattery: praising someone, or calling a wicked person good, when it is not true
The root of the word 'יקבהו'; it means to curse
Literally 'a nation'; here it is read as an unborn baby
'X means only Y': a formula that defines a word in a פסוק

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar says:
Any person who has flattery in him,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ עוּבָּרִין שֶׁבִּמְעֵי אִמָּן מְקַלְּלִין אוֹתוֹ,
phrases.english: even fetuses in their mothers' wombs curse him,
as it is stated: "He who says to the wicked: You are righteous,
peoples shall curse him, nations shall execrate him";
and "kov" means only a curse,
as it is stated: "Whom God has not cursed";
phrases.notes: במדבר 23:8. These are בלעם's words when he could not curse the Jewish people.

phrases.english: and "le'om" means only fetuses,
as it is stated: "And one people shall be stronger than the other people."
phrases.notes: בראשית 25:23. This was said about יעקב and עשו while they were still in רבקה's womb.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֲנוּפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next teaching of רבי אלעזר in the series that the memory sign listed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A flatterer is cursed even by unborn babies.

steps.title: A flatterer falls into גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a flatterer falls into גיהנם. He learns it from a פסוק in ישעיהו about people who call evil good, together with the fire described a few פסוקים later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Anyone who flatters falls into גיהנם. The פסוק says 'Woe to those who call evil good and good evil', and a few פסוקים later it says 'Therefore, as the tongue of fire eats straw and dry grass sinks in the flame', which shows they will burn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי אלעזר: a flatterer ends up in גיהנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling evil 'good' is exactly what a flatterer does. The punishment is taken from what the פסוק says next, fire burning straw, which points to the fire of גיהנם.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where the wicked are punished after death
'Woe': a word of warning in נביאים
'And so on': the rest of the פסוק continues
'What is written after it?': the proof comes from the next part of the passage

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֲנוּפָּה נוֹפֵל בְּגֵיהִנָּם,
phrases.english: Any person who has flattery in him falls into Gehenna,
as it is stated: "Woe to those who call evil good,
and good evil, etc."
What is written afterward?
"Therefore, as the tongue of fire devours straw,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 5:24. 'Afterward' here means a few פסוקים later, not the very next one.

phrases.english: and as the chaff is consumed by the flame, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֲנוּפָּה נוֹפֵל בְּגֵיהִנָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching in the same series by רבי אלעזר

steps.title: A flatterer ends up in the power of the one he flattered
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that whoever flatters someone will end up in that person's hands. If not his, then his children's, and if not theirs, his grandchild's. The proof starts with ירמיהו answering 'Amen' to חנניה, and the second פסוק comes on the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Whoever flatters another person will in the end fall into his hands. If not his, then his children's hands. If not his children's, then his grandson's hands. The proof is that ירמיהו the prophet said to חנניה, 'Amen, may ה׳ do so, may ה׳ carry out your words.' And it is written... (the second פסוק comes next).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the fourth teaching of רבי אלעזר, matching 'בידו' in the memory sign, and begins its proof. The proof is not finished yet: 'וכתיב' sets up a second פסוק that comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנניה was a false prophet. ירמיהו said 'Amen' to his words instead of openly rejecting them, and the גמרא treats that as a kind of flattery. The next פסוק will show who later had power over ירמיהו, finishing the proof that a flatterer falls into the hands of the other person's family.

keyTerms.meaning: Falls into his hands: ends up in his power
A false prophet in the time of ירמיהו
'And it is written': introduces another פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: This proof is not complete yet. The 'וכתיב' at the end leads into a second פסוק on the next part of the daf, so don't expect the conclusion here.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמַּחְנִיף לַחֲבֵירוֹ — סוֹף נוֹפֵל בְּיָדוֹ,
phrases.english: Anyone who flatters another ultimately falls into his hands.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵינוֹ נוֹפֵל בְּיָדוֹ — נוֹפֵל בְּיַד בָּנָיו,
phrases.english: And if he does not fall into his hands, he falls into his children's hands.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵינוֹ נוֹפֵל בְּיַד בָּנָיו — נוֹפֵל בְּיַד בֶּן בְּנוֹ,
phrases.english: And if he does not fall into his children's hands, he falls into his grandchild's hands,
as it is stated: "Then the prophet Jeremiah said to Hananiah:
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 28:5–6. The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: אָמֵן כֵּן יַעֲשֶׂה ה׳ יָקֵם ה׳ אֶת דְּבָרֶיךָ״,
phrases.english: Amen, the Lord should do so, the Lord should perform your words."
And it is written:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל הַמַּחְנִיף לַחֲבֵירוֹ

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A flatterer will fall into the power of the one he flattered, or of that person's children or grandchild.
